title.en: Derive assembly steps from a precedence graph

summary: Model which parts must precede which, then present any step sequence as a topological order of that graph.
objective: Ensure a demonstrated assembly or disassembly sequence is actually performable and that impossible orders are detected.
applies_when: A scene teaches how something is built, installed, serviced or taken apart.
Steps are numbered, or a next and previous control walks through an assembly.
Several subassemblies could be built in different orders.
intent_signals: in what order does it go together
example_prompts: Walk through building the camera rig step by step.
Show which parts have to come off before the battery can be replaced.
negative_signals: Free exploration of a finished object where no order is implied.
Purely decorative build-up animations that make no procedural claim.
not_for: Free exploration of a finished object where no order is implied.
Purely decorative build-up animations that make no procedural claim.

principles: An ordering claim is a graph claim. Constraints such as the fastener needing its bracket, or the cover needing everything beneath it, are directed edges between parts.

A directed graph has a topological order exactly when it contains no directed cycle, so a set of precedence constraints with a cycle describes an assembly that cannot be built in that decomposition, which is information worth surfacing rather than hiding.

The presented sequence is one valid order. How many others exist depends on the constraints: a chain of dependencies admits exactly one topological order, while independent branches leave genuinely unordered steps. Presenting a sequence as the order hides that freedom where it exists and makes the model brittle when a part is added.
Disassembly is not automatically the reverse: fasteners, adhesives and captive parts break the symmetry, so the reverse order needs its own check.
implementation: Record precedence as explicit pairs on the part data, with a short reason such as blocked path, fastened by, or supports.
Generate the presented sequence from the graph rather than hand-numbering steps, so adding a part updates the walkthrough.
Detect a cycle and report it as an unbuildable constraint set, naming the parts in the cycle instead of silently choosing an order.
Where several orders are valid, either group independent steps as parallel or state that the order shown is one of several.
Derive the explode offsets and the step camera framing from the same graph so the visual separation matches the stated order.
observable_checks: Step through the sequence and confirm each part has a clear path into place with the parts already installed; a part that must pass through solid geometry indicates a missing constraint.
Introduce a deliberate cycle in the test data and confirm the tool reports it rather than producing an arbitrary sequence.
Reverse the sequence and check the removal story separately, especially around fasteners and captive parts.

Add a new part with one constraint and confirm the numbering updates without manual renumbering; where the constraints are a chain, confirm the tool reports a single valid order rather than offering alternatives that do not exist.

creative_affordances: Presentation is free: exploded stills, animated inserts, ghosted future parts or a hand-drawn manual style all satisfy the same graph.
A story-driven build sequence may reorder independent steps for pacing, since independent steps are genuinely unordered.
known_limits: Authored procedural guidance with a cited graph-theoretic fact; no real product assembly has been validated here.
Physical feasibility also depends on tool access, clearance and handling, which this rule does not model.

claims.statement: A topological order arranges the vertices of a digraph so that every directed edge points from an earlier vertex to a later one, and a digraph has a topological order if and only if it is a directed acyclic graph.
claims.scope: Property of finite directed graphs; it constrains orderings of a precedence model, not the physical feasibility of any assembly step.

source_refs.locator: Topological sort; proposition relating topological order and directed acyclic graphs
